title: Uncovering Banking Phishing Infrastructure via Certificate Transparency Logs
context: Before launching credential-harvesting emails against a regional financial institution, threat actors registered 18 lookalike domains and issued free automated TLS certificates so victims would see a browser padlock.
methodology: Defenders monitored public Certificate Transparency logs (crt.sh) for brand substrings and common homoglyphs without touching external hosts.
Extracted Subject Alternative Names (SANs) from newly issued certificates, revealing 11 additional sibling domains bundled on the same X.509 certificate.
Correlated historical passive DNS resolutions and ASN allocations via Hurricane Electric BGP Toolkit, identifying a single bulletproof VPS subnet.
Inspected pre-existing urlscan.io snapshots to confirm identical login-kit CSS hashes without sending live analyst traffic.
lessons: TLS encryption does not imply legitimacy. Because Certificate Authorities must log certificates publicly in append-only CT Merkle trees, defenders can detect phishing domains hours before the first lure email is sent.

title: Verifying Recycled Footage Using SunCalc & Historical Weather Data
context: A viral video purported to show an industrial explosion occurring at 08:30 local time in winter, sparking commodity market rumors.
methodology: Extracted crisp video keyframes using the InVID Verification Plugin and performed reverse image searches on Yandex Images and TinEye.
TinEye sorted by 'Oldest' surfaced zero prior exact matches, requiring primary geospatial and temporal verification.
Matched three distinctive cooling towers and a rail overpass in OpenStreetMap Overpass Turbo to pinpoint exact coordinates.

Measured shadow azimuth cast by a vertical light pole (cast toward the northeast) and checked SunCalc for the claimed winter morning date—proving the sun could only cast that shadow angle in late afternoon during summer, matching a documented training drill two years prior.
lessons: Geolocation ('where') is only half of verification; chronolocation ('when') prevents authentic old footage from being weaponized in new contexts.

title: Detecting Maritime AIS Transponder Gaps with Sentinel-1 SAR Imagery
sourceOrg: Open-Source Maritime Compliance Research (Bellingcat / Public Environmental NGOs)
context: Cargo vessels suspected of unauthorized ship-to-ship oil transfers turned off their Automatic Identification System (AIS) transponders ('going dark') for 36 hours in international waters.
methodology: Recorded the last known public AIS speed, heading, and timestamp to calculate a maximum search radius polygon.
Queried the European Space Agency Copernicus Browser for Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) passes, which penetrate cloud cover and darkness.
Identified bright metallic radar reflections of two stationary vessels side-by-side inside the calculated drift zone.
Cross-checked subsequent Sentinel-2 optical imagery on a clear day to measure hull length and deck crane configuration.
lessons: When digital telemetry (AIS) disappears, physical earth-observation sensors (SAR radar and optical satellites) provide independent, non-spoofable corroboration.

title: Auditing Legacy Attack Surface Through Wayback CDX & Passive DNS
context: During an authorized passive-only security review, a software company believed all legacy staging documentation portals had been decommissioned.
methodology: Queried the Internet Archive CDX API for `*.company-example` URLs captured over the past eight years, returning passive plain-text URL inventories.
Filtered archived URLs locally with `grep` and `sort -u` for `.pdf`, `.json`, and `/api/v1/` documentation paths.
Cross-referenced discovered hostnames against SecurityTrails passive DNS to distinguish retired CNAMEs (dangling subdomain takeover candidates) from active IPs.
Delivered a prioritized remediation list without sending a single HTTP request to the client's servers.
lessons: Decommissioning a link on a homepage does not erase historical crawl indexes or dangling CNAME records.

title: Identifying Unintended Internal Path Leaks in Public PDF Publications
context: An organization published 40 quarterly investor PDF brochures on its public press page without sanitizing document properties.
methodology: Downloaded publicly linked press PDFs inside an isolated research VM and inspected them locally offline with ExifTool.
Extracted `CreatorTool`, `Producer`, and `Author` XMP fields revealing exact macOS/Windows build versions, internal Active Directory usernames (`jsmith`), and local network share paths.
Mapped the email format (`first_initial + last_name`) against public MX and SPF records to demonstrate spear-phishing exposure.
Implemented an automated CI/CD ExifTool metadata-stripping gate prior to public file uploads.
lessons: Publicly downloadable documents routinely leak internal usernames and software patch levels needed for MITRE ATT&CK T1589/T1592.

title: Pivoting Across Command-and-Control Servers via Favicon Hashes in Shodan
context: A SOC team blocked a single Cobalt Strike / phishing management IP observed in an outbound proxy alert, wanting to proactively identify sibling servers in the same campaign.
methodology: Queried the blocked IP in Shodan and Censys passive indexes rather than probing the live server.
Noted a distinctive non-standard HTTP `favicon.ico` MurmurHash3 value and a custom self-signed TLS issuer string.
Pivoted in Shodan on `http.favicon.hash` combined with the TLS serial pattern, uncovering 14 unblocked servers deployed across three hosting providers in the past 72 hours.
Exported defanged IOCs (`hxxp://`, `[.]`) with TLP:AMBER+STRICT markings into MISP and SIEM blocklists.
lessons: Blocking a single IP sits at the bottom of the Pyramid of Pain; pivoting on infrastructure artifacts (favicon hashes, TLS certificates) uncovers entire adversary clusters.

title: Triaging Midnight Port-Scan Alerts Using GreyNoise & RIPEstat
context: A junior SOC analyst received 120 firewall alerts at 02:00 UTC showing inbound TCP/443 requests with unusual User-Agent headers against edge load balancers.
methodology: Extracted unique source IPs using CLI `sort | uniq -c` and checked them in GreyNoise Visualizer.
Confirmed 118 of the 120 IPs belonged to verified benign academic and internet-census scanners (Censys and Shadowserver) scanning the entire IPv4 space.
Investigated the remaining 2 IPs—absent from benign scanner lists—in Abuse.ch ThreatFox, RIPEstat, and VirusTotal passive DNS.
Discovered those 2 IPs were exclusively targeting a newly disclosed CVE listed in CISA KEV, escalating a focused P1 incident ticket within 12 minutes.
lessons: Separating mass internet background noise from targeted exploitation is one of the highest-impact OSINT skills for SOC L1 analysts.

title: Tracing Cross-Border Shell Subsidiaries Using GLEIF LEI & Companies House
context: A procurement team needed to verify whether a newly incorporated European electronics distributor was covertly controlled by a sanctioned parent conglomerate.
methodology: Looked up the vendor's Legal Entity Identifier in GLEIF Search to inspect Level 2 'Direct Accounting Consolidating Parent' disclosures.
Traced UK intermediary holding companies in UK Companies House, reviewing historical Persons with Significant Control (PSC) filings and shared registered office addresses.
Cross-checked past and current corporate officers against OpenSanctions (OFAC/EU consolidated lists), corroborating exact date-of-birth and middle-name transliterations.
Documented an evidence chain backed exclusively by primary statutory PDFs with Admiralty A1 grading.
lessons: Corporate due diligence relies on primary statutory registries and unique entity identifiers (LEIs, company numbers) rather than name-only searches.

title: Environmental Supply-Chain Verification with Optical Satellite Timelines
context: An agricultural supplier certified that zero protected forest land had been cleared after a statutory cutoff date.
methodology: Located concession boundary coordinates published in public ministry gazettes and imported the polygon into OpenStreetMap / Google Earth.
Reviewed monthly Sentinel-2 false-color infrared composites in Copernicus Browser (where healthy vegetation appears bright crimson and bare cleared soil appears grey-brown).
Pinpointed the exact two-week window when haul roads and clearing appeared—eight months after the pledged cutoff date.
Archived every ministry PDF and satellite tile date to ensure full reproducibility by independent auditors.
lessons: Multi-spectral satellite archives allow anyone to audit environmental and infrastructure claims across multi-year timelines.

title: Avoiding False-Flag Attribution Bias with ACH & Admiralty Grading
context: During a website defacement incident, attackers left Cyrillic strings in HTML comments and routed traffic through an Eastern European VPN exit node, prompting hasty verbal claims of nation-state attribution.
methodology: Constructed an Analysis of Competing Hypotheses (ACH) matrix testing three hypotheses: H1 State Actor, H2 Financially Motivated Cybercrime Group, H3 Opportunistic Script Kiddie using public defacement templates.
Searched the exact HTML template hash on GitHub and Wayback archives, finding it was a 6-year-old public forum template with untouched default comments.
Checked CISA KEV and server logs, showing exploitation of an unpatched 2-year-old CMS plugin scanned globally weeks earlier.
Issued a BLUF executive brief grading attribution to a state actor as 'Highly Improbable' and focusing remediation on CMS patch governance.
lessons: Technical artifacts like language strings and VPN exit IPs are trivially spoofed; ACH protects analysts from confirmation bias.
